title: Stratified kernel throttle + prefill horizon estimator
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight 'stratified kernel throttle' layer that uses a short-horizon prefill estimator to choose safe kernel fallbacks under variable sequence-length/architecture conditions. Goal: reduce latency tail spikes from mis-selected kernels during mixed-prefill/decode bursts while retaining cost-efficient kernel choices for steady-state traffic.
motivation: We observe sporadic 95/99th latency regressions for mixed-prefill workloads when the kernel selector over-commits to aggressive, high-occupancy kernels based on stale seqlen averages. This ticket proposes an additional runtime guard: a quick prefill horizon estimator (50-200ms window) that stratifies requests and temporarily throttles aggressive kernels until warmed evidence accumulates. This reduces tail latency regressions for conversational bursts and improves SLA stability for Dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: Prefill horizon estimator implemented and exposed via runtime flag
Stratified kernel throttle integrates with kernel selector decision path and can apply conservative kernel overrides for short time windows
E2E tests show 30-60% reduction in 95/99 latency spikes on synthetic mixed-prefill traces compared to baseline
No more than 5% average throughput regression on steady-state small-seqlen synthetic load
Telemetry dashboards surface throttle events, prefill horizon estimates, and per-kernel latency impact
design_notes: Estimator approach: streaming exponential moving average + short burst detector tuned to 50-200ms horizons to avoid long cold starts
Strata: three strata (conservative, default, aggressive) determined by estimated token-phase volatility and host occupancy; conservative maps to quantized/low-occupancy kernel variants
Throttle policy: soft override with decay; if estimator confidence is low, bias toward conservative choice for next N requests or until warm counters reach threshold
Interface: small runtime API hook that returns kernel tier preference and confidence; selector can apply override when confidence < threshold or when throttle offset active
Fallbacks: telemetry-driven rollback rule that disables throttle if tail latency increases or cost increases beyond configured guardrails
implementation_steps: Prototype estimator library with synthetic trace replayer (unit: 3 days)
Add runtime hook and selector integration (unit: 4 days)
Add metrics (throttle_count, estimator_confidence, strata_histogram, kernel_switches) and wire to Console (unit: 2 days)
Create e2e benchmark harness using conv-burst traces and run regression matrix across GPU types (unit: 3 days)
Ship behind feature flag and run canary on Dedicated pool for 48h (unit: 1 day)
Iterate based on canary telemetry and finalize rollout (unit: 2 days)
telemetry_requirements: throttle_event {timestamp, pod_id, model, requested_seqlen, estimated_horizon_ms, chosen_stratum, previous_kernel}
trace samples for cases where throttle fired and request latency > SLA
test_plan: Unit tests for estimator smoothing and burst detector edge cases
Simulated traces: conv-burst, mixed-short-long, adversarial-long-prefill sequences
Hardware matrix: A100, H100, and an entry-level GPU to validate stratification differences
Chaos test: random network delay and sudden load spikes to ensure decay logic prevents oscillation
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-conservative throttling may hurt throughput and cost per token. Mitigation: Tiered rollout with strict cost regression guard in canary, and soft override semantics
Risk: Estimator miscalibration across regions/hardware. Mitigation: Expose config knobs per pool and capture per-host histograms to autodetect miscalibration
Risk: Selector complexity increase leads to hard-to-debug regressions. Mitigation: Add detailed trace logging and a selector-mode telemetry flag to reproduce decisions
open_questions: What default horizon window should we ship with? (50ms vs 200ms trade-offs)
Should strata be static mappings or continuously learned per-customer?
How to balance cost guardrails for Hosted vs Dedicated customers?
notes: Related reading: kernel selection instability post rolling upgrade discovered in incident INC-2025-02-kerneldrift
Initial microbench results attached to PR: https://github.com/redwood/re/runtime/pull/2345
